hushtelegram.title: v0.0.24
hushtelegram.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.24 has 69 patches for the Google Play build of Telegram 13.2.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72911) and telegram.org's Telegram 13.2.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72809). The 13.1 builds aren't supported anymore, so update Telegram before you patch. It's on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, which needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. Most of it came from your reports again, and it changes something for #2, #7, #34, #35, #37, #50, #53, #54, #56, #59, #60 and #61. Special contacts keeps a history of the people you choose to track. The phone number screen can sign you in on Telegram's test servers or with a bot token, and another new switch lets screenshots work in chats that don't allow saving. New switches start off, except `Keep the Keep-Alive Service running`, which only does anything while Telegram's own Keep-Alive Service is on.

New in this release

- `Special contacts`, a new switch under `Show user and chat IDs` in HushTelegram settings > Look and feel, off by default. With it on, a person's profile menu gets `Track this user`, and from then on HushTelegram keeps a history of what Telegram already shows you about them. That covers coming online and going offline, typing, and changes to their name, username, phone number or profile photo. It also notes when you save or remove them as a contact, and when they add you back or drop you. Telegram never says when someone blocks you, so that line is a guess, written when their photo and last seen disappear together. The `Tracked people` row under the switch lists everyone, newest activity first. Tap a person to read their history, clear it or stop tracking them. Each account can track up to 50 people, the newest 500 lines are kept for each, and nothing leaves the phone. (#53)

- `Ghost mode button`, under Ghost mode in Privacy and off by default. It puts a ghost at the top of the chat list, next to Telegram's own buttons, and one tap turns Ghost mode on or off with a short message saying which. The ghost is filled while Ghost mode is on and just an outline while it's off. It steps aside while search is open.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save to Gallery to stories`, off by default. A story's three-dot menu gets Telegram's own Save to Gallery without Premium, on stories that don't allow saving too. It saves only the ones you pick.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Allow screenshots in chats that don't allow saving`, off by default. Screenshots and screen recordings stop coming out black in those chats and channels, in their photos and videos, on their profiles and in protected stories. Telegram doesn't tell anyone you took one. Secret chats, view-once media and the passcode screen stay blocked. (#34)

- `Save downloaded files` has a `What to copy` row right under its switch. Tick documents, music, photos, videos or voice messages, and only those kinds get a copy in Download/Telegram. Everything is ticked to start, so nothing changes until you untick something.

- `Keep videos muted on volume keys` has a new switch, `Start videos without sound`, off by default. A video you open plays muted, so it won't blast out in public or cut over your music. Press a volume key and that video gets its sound. The next one you open starts quiet again. Round videos keep their sound. (#61)

- `Disable double-tap reactions` has a new switch, `Hide the emoji pack line`, off by default. It takes the line that says a message contains emoji from some pack off the bottom of the long-press menu, along with the gap above it.

- `Move All Chats`, under the folder tabs settings. It starts off. With it on, an account without Premium can drag All Chats to another place among its folder tabs, and it stays there after a restart. The place is kept on this phone for this account, so your other devices still show All Chats first.

- `Fit all folder tabs` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. With lots of folders, the tabs above the chat list shrink until every one of them fits on the screen, so you don't have to scroll sideways to find one. They stop shrinking at a size that's still readable, and with only a few folders nothing changes. (#53)

- `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` has a `Folder in internal storage` row under it, so Telegram's files can go in a folder you name, like Internal storage/Plus, instead of Internal storage/Telegram. Changing the name takes a restart, and files in the folder you used before stay there and still open. Leave it empty for Telegram. (#7)

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Clear from cache to the message menu`, off by default. A video or file message gets a Clear from cache item. It stops a running download, deletes what Telegram kept of it and brings the download arrow back. A toast says how much was cleared, and copies you saved to Downloads or Pictures stay.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save album art to the message menu`, off by default. A song with art, inside the file or on Telegram, gets a Save album art item that puts the picture in Pictures.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save video cover to the message menu`, off by default. A video gets a Save video cover item that puts its biggest cover or thumbnail in Pictures, fetching it first if it isn't on the phone yet.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Forward to Saved Messages to the message menu`, off by default. A message you can forward gets a Forward to Saved Messages item in its long-press menu. Pick as is, without the sender's name, without the caption, or both, and it lands in your Saved Messages at once.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Fast forward to the message menu`, off by default. A message you can forward gets a Fast forward item in its long-press menu. Pick without the sender's name, without the caption, or both, then pick a chat, and it goes out at once.

- `Strip link tracking` has a new switch, `Clean links when you copy or paste`, off by default. Copy a link in Telegram, or paste one into the message box, and tags like utm_source and fbclid come off. Only text that is one link and nothing else changes. Find it in HushTelegram settings > More settings > Links. (#53)

- `Faster downloads` has a third switch, `Faster uploads`, off by default. An upload keeps four times as many pieces on their way at once, up to 64. Telegram's servers still decide how fast an account can send, and the piece size and file size limits don't change. Find it in HushTelegram settings > Playback. (#53)

- `Hide popular apps` has a new switch, `Disable secret chats`, off by default. When someone asks for a secret chat, the phone ignores the request. Nothing is saved or shown and nothing is sent back, so the other person just sees it waiting. Secret chats you already have keep working. Find it in HushTelegram settings > Ads. (#53)

- `Sort chats by date` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default, with a second one, `Oldest chats first`. Your unpinned chats line up by the date of their last message, newest or oldest first. Pinned chats and the archive row stay where they are, and nothing is sent to Telegram, so it only changes this phone's list. (#53)

- `Passcode for hidden chats` is a new switch under `Hide picked chats`, off by default. With it on, opening `Chats to hide`, turning off `Hide picked chats` and turning the switch itself off all ask for your Telegram passcode first. It guards this settings page only, so search still finds the hidden chats. Telegram needs a passcode set before it will turn on. (#53)

- `Administrators row in the side menu` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. It adds an `Administrators` row to the side menu. One tap lists only the groups and channels you own or manage, and the row then reads `Show all chats` to bring the rest back. It only changes this phone's list and starts off again when Telegram restarts. (#53)

- `Hide accounts` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. The accounts you tick in `Accounts to hide` leave Telegram's account lists, and only there. Each one stays signed in, keeps syncing, and its notifications follow Telegram's own settings. Nothing is signed out or deleted, the account you're using always shows, and at least one account always stays. An optional `Passcode for hidden accounts` switch asks for your Telegram passcode before the list opens. (#53)

- `Stop usage reports` now also holds `Receive only mode` and `Power off accounts`, both off by default. Pick accounts under each switch in HushTelegram settings > Privacy. A receive only account reads, downloads and marks chats read, but messages, reactions, drafts and typing stay on the phone and show an error. A powered off account sends nothing, and its name in the side menu gets an (Off) tag. Telegram's connection can stay open in the background, so a powered off account may still receive messages and notifications. (#53)

- `Use normal paste` has a new switch, `Mention by ID`, off by default. Type @ and a user's ID number, or tg://user?id= and the ID, in the message box and it goes out as a real mention. It only works for people the app has already seen, in a chat or a group. For anyone else the text stays as you typed it and a short note says so. Turn it on in HushTelegram settings > Conversations.

- `Faster downloads` has a third switch, `Download manager`, off by default. Files download one at a time, in the order you asked for them, instead of several at once. A `Downloads` row in the side menu (turn on `Side menu` too) lists what's downloading, what's waiting and what's finished, with a Cancel for each file still going. A file you open or play still jumps the line. (#53)

- `Voice messages in the music player` has a new switch, `Remember where playback stopped`, off by default. Videos, voice messages and music pick up where you left off, even short ones. Telegram only does that for long ones. Turn it off and everything plays as Telegram plays it. (#53)

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Select between`, off by default. It adds a button to the bar that shows while you pick messages. Tap it and everything between the first and last message you picked gets selected. Pick one past the end and the gap fills in. It stops at Telegram's 100 message limit. (#53)

- `Folder icons` is a new row with the folder tab settings. Pick Regular, Bold or Filled and HushTelegram draws a small icon beside each folder in its own lists, like Folder to open. A folder called Work gets a briefcase, Friends a group, and a name it doesn't know gets a plain folder. Telegram's own folder tabs stay as they are. The icons are from Phosphor Icons (MIT). Off by default. (#53)

- `HushTelegram icon and name` has a fourth `Icon style`, `Telegram's own icon`. Pick it with an `App name` and Telegram keeps its usual icon, with only the name under it changed. (#37)

- `Test server sign-in`, under Chat list and off by default. When you sign in or add an account, the phone number screen shows Telegram's own Test Backend box. Tick it to sign that account in on Telegram's test servers, kept apart from your other accounts. Untick it to go back. With the box ticked, the phone screen also takes Telegram's test numbers (+999 66 X YYYY), which the regular app turns away as an unknown country code. (#59)

- `Translate with an outside service` adds `Translate into` to a chat's three-dot menu, right under Translate this chat. It opens the same language list as the settings row, so you can switch between your language and English without leaving the chat. Pick one and the chat is written again in it. (#35)

- `Bot token sign-in`, under Chat list and off by default. Turn it on and the phone number screen gets a `Sign in with a bot token` button, both on first sign-in and when you add an account. Paste the token @BotFather gave your bot and that account signs in as the bot. A wrong or revoked token gets a short message and the box stays open so you can fix it. Chats show up as people message the bot and you can answer them, but there's no older history, and a bot has no contacts, stickers or folders. A bot with a webhook set, or one another program is already reading, may not get its messages here. (#53)

Fixes

- `Import settings` no longer says nothing will change for a file that only picks other folder icons. It lists the change and offers to import it.

- `Hide sponsored proxy channel` works the moment you flip it. The proxy's channel used to stay in the chat list until the next message or update came in.

- `Hide Premium, gifts and Stars` now takes Send a Gift out of the three-dot menu on profiles and channels too. It was still sitting there with the switch on.

- If you hide a pinned chat and unpin it on another device, the unpin now sticks. Hidden pins also count toward your pin limit here, so you see Telegram's limit message instead of a pin the server would turn down.

- When Google sign-in fails on Telegram's login email screen, a short message now points at the email box. Telegram used to just stay on the screen after you picked an account, and a patched copy can't get past Google there.

- If you use Telegram's Keep-Alive Service instead of push, messages no longer wait until you open the app. Android stopped that service about a minute after you left Telegram. Now it runs with a quiet notification and keeps going. A new switch under `Repair Firebase push registration`, `Keep the Keep-Alive Service running`, is on by default and only matters while Keep-Alive Service is on in Telegram's own settings. (#50, #54)

- `Keep deleted messages` now saves a kept photo, and any kept file or video up to 20 MB, the moment the sender deletes it. Before, a photo you hadn't opened yet just spun forever, because Telegram can't fetch a deleted message's file later. (#2)

- `Disable update checks` now hides the Update Telegram bar even when Telegram found the update before you turned the switch on. The bar used to stay, since Telegram only forgets an update when a later check comes back empty. (#60)

- With `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` on, the photos and videos Telegram downloads no longer fill up the phone's gallery. The folder now gets a .nomedia file, so the gallery only shows what you save to it yourself. (#60)

- `Hide greeting stickers` now also hides the custom sticker a Premium or Business user picks for their intro, the one you see when you open an empty chat with them. Only the preview of your own intro, while you edit it, keeps its sticker. (#56)

- In the `Side menu`, New Message has a pencil beside it again. Telegram 13 turned the old message icon into an eye, so the row looked like it would show you something.

Other changes

- Moved to Telegram 13.2. telegram.org's build is 13.2.0 (version code 72809) and the Google Play build is 13.2.1 (version code 72911). The 13.1 builds aren't supported anymore, so update Telegram before you patch.

- `Hide the reaction picker` now covers the bubble of reactions that pops up over a selected message too, so tapping a post to pick it for a reply or a forward can't land on a reaction.

- `Hide picked chats` now also takes hidden chats out of the forward picker, the share sheet and quick share. Saved Messages always stays in those lists.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.5.0 or newer. 0.0.23 only needed 2.3.0, so update Manager first if that's what you patched with.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get the right Telegram. From Google Play that's 13.2.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72911), which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. From telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) it's 13.2.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72809). The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from 0.0.23? Get 13.2 from the same place you got 13.1 (Google Play or telegram.org), patch it and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. Your settings and chats stay. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. On phones where Firebase notifications don't come through, try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy. It turns those two on for you unless you've set them yourself.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The Ways in section on that page decides which of those (plus the side menu row and the icon shortcut) stay.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

What was checked

All 2048 runtime tests passed locally, and all 625 patch tests passed too (162 unit tests and 463 that patch the real Telegram APKs), along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 69 patches applied without forcing to telegram.org's Telegram 13.2.0 (version code 72809) and to the Google Play build of 13.2.1 (version code 72911). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, resource table, native libraries and zip alignment.

Both builds were patched from this exact bundle and installed over the HushTelegram already on a Galaxy S25, without clearing its data. Both were signed in to Telegram. On each one the walk opened Telegram's Settings, Privacy, Folders and Themes pages and a channel, then every section of the HushTelegram settings and the Changed switches page. That's 22 screens per build, with no crash and no problem found on either.

The new `Allow screenshots in chats that don't allow saving` switch was checked on the same phone. With it off, a bot message that blocks saving and a channel with Restrict saving content both came out black in screenshots, same as stock Telegram. With it on, both showed normally.

## [2.1.1](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-desktop/compare/v2.1.0...v2.1.1) (2026-11-06)


### Bug Fixes

repos.title: v0.0.24
repos.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.24 has 69 patches for the Google Play build of Telegram 13.2.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72911) and telegram.org's Telegram 13.2.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72809). The 13.1 builds aren't supported anymore, so update Telegram before you patch. It's on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, which needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. Most of it came from your reports again, and it changes something for #2, #7, #34, #35, #37, #50, #53, #54, #56, #59, #60 and #61. Special contacts keeps a history of the people you choose to track. The phone number screen can sign you in on Telegram's test servers or with a bot token, and another new switch lets screenshots work in chats that don't allow saving. New switches start off, except `Keep the Keep-Alive Service running`, which only does anything while Telegram's own Keep-Alive Service is on.

New in this release

- `Special contacts`, a new switch under `Show user and chat IDs` in HushTelegram settings > Look and feel, off by default. With it on, a person's profile menu gets `Track this user`, and from then on HushTelegram keeps a history of what Telegram already shows you about them. That covers coming online and going offline, typing, and changes to their name, username, phone number or profile photo. It also notes when you save or remove them as a contact, and when they add you back or drop you. Telegram never says when someone blocks you, so that line is a guess, written when their photo and last seen disappear together. The `Tracked people` row under the switch lists everyone, newest activity first. Tap a person to read their history, clear it or stop tracking them. Each account can track up to 50 people, the newest 500 lines are kept for each, and nothing leaves the phone. (#53)

- `Ghost mode button`, under Ghost mode in Privacy and off by default. It puts a ghost at the top of the chat list, next to Telegram's own buttons, and one tap turns Ghost mode on or off with a short message saying which. The ghost is filled while Ghost mode is on and just an outline while it's off. It steps aside while search is open.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save to Gallery to stories`, off by default. A story's three-dot menu gets Telegram's own Save to Gallery without Premium, on stories that don't allow saving too. It saves only the ones you pick.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Allow screenshots in chats that don't allow saving`, off by default. Screenshots and screen recordings stop coming out black in those chats and channels, in their photos and videos, on their profiles and in protected stories. Telegram doesn't tell anyone you took one. Secret chats, view-once media and the passcode screen stay blocked. (#34)

- `Save downloaded files` has a `What to copy` row right under its switch. Tick documents, music, photos, videos or voice messages, and only those kinds get a copy in Download/Telegram. Everything is ticked to start, so nothing changes until you untick something.

- `Keep videos muted on volume keys` has a new switch, `Start videos without sound`, off by default. A video you open plays muted, so it won't blast out in public or cut over your music. Press a volume key and that video gets its sound. The next one you open starts quiet again. Round videos keep their sound. (#61)

- `Disable double-tap reactions` has a new switch, `Hide the emoji pack line`, off by default. It takes the line that says a message contains emoji from some pack off the bottom of the long-press menu, along with the gap above it.

- `Move All Chats`, under the folder tabs settings. It starts off. With it on, an account without Premium can drag All Chats to another place among its folder tabs, and it stays there after a restart. The place is kept on this phone for this account, so your other devices still show All Chats first.

- `Fit all folder tabs` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. With lots of folders, the tabs above the chat list shrink until every one of them fits on the screen, so you don't have to scroll sideways to find one. They stop shrinking at a size that's still readable, and with only a few folders nothing changes. (#53)

- `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` has a `Folder in internal storage` row under it, so Telegram's files can go in a folder you name, like Internal storage/Plus, instead of Internal storage/Telegram. Changing the name takes a restart, and files in the folder you used before stay there and still open. Leave it empty for Telegram. (#7)

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Clear from cache to the message menu`, off by default. A video or file message gets a Clear from cache item. It stops a running download, deletes what Telegram kept of it and brings the download arrow back. A toast says how much was cleared, and copies you saved to Downloads or Pictures stay.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save album art to the message menu`, off by default. A song with art, inside the file or on Telegram, gets a Save album art item that puts the picture in Pictures.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Save video cover to the message menu`, off by default. A video gets a Save video cover item that puts its biggest cover or thumbnail in Pictures, fetching it first if it isn't on the phone yet.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Forward to Saved Messages to the message menu`, off by default. A message you can forward gets a Forward to Saved Messages item in its long-press menu. Pick as is, without the sender's name, without the caption, or both, and it lands in your Saved Messages at once.

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Add Fast forward to the message menu`, off by default. A message you can forward gets a Fast forward item in its long-press menu. Pick without the sender's name, without the caption, or both, then pick a chat, and it goes out at once.

- `Strip link tracking` has a new switch, `Clean links when you copy or paste`, off by default. Copy a link in Telegram, or paste one into the message box, and tags like utm_source and fbclid come off. Only text that is one link and nothing else changes. Find it in HushTelegram settings > More settings > Links. (#53)

- `Faster downloads` has a third switch, `Faster uploads`, off by default. An upload keeps four times as many pieces on their way at once, up to 64. Telegram's servers still decide how fast an account can send, and the piece size and file size limits don't change. Find it in HushTelegram settings > Playback. (#53)

- `Hide popular apps` has a new switch, `Disable secret chats`, off by default. When someone asks for a secret chat, the phone ignores the request. Nothing is saved or shown and nothing is sent back, so the other person just sees it waiting. Secret chats you already have keep working. Find it in HushTelegram settings > Ads. (#53)

- `Sort chats by date` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default, with a second one, `Oldest chats first`. Your unpinned chats line up by the date of their last message, newest or oldest first. Pinned chats and the archive row stay where they are, and nothing is sent to Telegram, so it only changes this phone's list. (#53)

- `Passcode for hidden chats` is a new switch under `Hide picked chats`, off by default. With it on, opening `Chats to hide`, turning off `Hide picked chats` and turning the switch itself off all ask for your Telegram passcode first. It guards this settings page only, so search still finds the hidden chats. Telegram needs a passcode set before it will turn on. (#53)

- `Administrators row in the side menu` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. It adds an `Administrators` row to the side menu. One tap lists only the groups and channels you own or manage, and the row then reads `Show all chats` to bring the rest back. It only changes this phone's list and starts off again when Telegram restarts. (#53)

- `Hide accounts` is a new switch under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. The accounts you tick in `Accounts to hide` leave Telegram's account lists, and only there. Each one stays signed in, keeps syncing, and its notifications follow Telegram's own settings. Nothing is signed out or deleted, the account you're using always shows, and at least one account always stays. An optional `Passcode for hidden accounts` switch asks for your Telegram passcode before the list opens. (#53)

- `Stop usage reports` now also holds `Receive only mode` and `Power off accounts`, both off by default. Pick accounts under each switch in HushTelegram settings > Privacy. A receive only account reads, downloads and marks chats read, but messages, reactions, drafts and typing stay on the phone and show an error. A powered off account sends nothing, and its name in the side menu gets an (Off) tag. Telegram's connection can stay open in the background, so a powered off account may still receive messages and notifications. (#53)

- `Use normal paste` has a new switch, `Mention by ID`, off by default. Type @ and a user's ID number, or tg://user?id= and the ID, in the message box and it goes out as a real mention. It only works for people the app has already seen, in a chat or a group. For anyone else the text stays as you typed it and a short note says so. Turn it on in HushTelegram settings > Conversations.

- `Faster downloads` has a third switch, `Download manager`, off by default. Files download one at a time, in the order you asked for them, instead of several at once. A `Downloads` row in the side menu (turn on `Side menu` too) lists what's downloading, what's waiting and what's finished, with a Cancel for each file still going. A file you open or play still jumps the line. (#53)

- `Voice messages in the music player` has a new switch, `Remember where playback stopped`, off by default. Videos, voice messages and music pick up where you left off, even short ones. Telegram only does that for long ones. Turn it off and everything plays as Telegram plays it. (#53)

- `Add Repeat to the message menu` has a new switch, `Select between`, off by default. It adds a button to the bar that shows while you pick messages. Tap it and everything between the first and last message you picked gets selected. Pick one past the end and the gap fills in. It stops at Telegram's 100 message limit. (#53)

- `Folder icons` is a new row with the folder tab settings. Pick Regular, Bold or Filled and HushTelegram draws a small icon beside each folder in its own lists, like Folder to open. A folder called Work gets a briefcase, Friends a group, and a name it doesn't know gets a plain folder. Telegram's own folder tabs stay as they are. The icons are from Phosphor Icons (MIT). Off by default. (#53)

- `HushTelegram icon and name` has a fourth `Icon style`, `Telegram's own icon`. Pick it with an `App name` and Telegram keeps its usual icon, with only the name under it changed. (#37)

- `Test server sign-in`, under Chat list and off by default. When you sign in or add an account, the phone number screen shows Telegram's own Test Backend box. Tick it to sign that account in on Telegram's test servers, kept apart from your other accounts. Untick it to go back. With the box ticked, the phone screen also takes Telegram's test numbers (+999 66 X YYYY), which the regular app turns away as an unknown country code. (#59)

- `Translate with an outside service` adds `Translate into` to a chat's three-dot menu, right under Translate this chat. It opens the same language list as the settings row, so you can switch between your language and English without leaving the chat. Pick one and the chat is written again in it. (#35)

- `Bot token sign-in`, under Chat list and off by default. Turn it on and the phone number screen gets a `Sign in with a bot token` button, both on first sign-in and when you add an account. Paste the token @BotFather gave your bot and that account signs in as the bot. A wrong or revoked token gets a short message and the box stays open so you can fix it. Chats show up as people message the bot and you can answer them, but there's no older history, and a bot has no contacts, stickers or folders. A bot with a webhook set, or one another program is already reading, may not get its messages here. (#53)

Fixes

- `Import settings` no longer says nothing will change for a file that only picks other folder icons. It lists the change and offers to import it.

- `Hide sponsored proxy channel` works the moment you flip it. The proxy's channel used to stay in the chat list until the next message or update came in.

- `Hide Premium, gifts and Stars` now takes Send a Gift out of the three-dot menu on profiles and channels too. It was still sitting there with the switch on.

- If you hide a pinned chat and unpin it on another device, the unpin now sticks. Hidden pins also count toward your pin limit here, so you see Telegram's limit message instead of a pin the server would turn down.

- When Google sign-in fails on Telegram's login email screen, a short message now points at the email box. Telegram used to just stay on the screen after you picked an account, and a patched copy can't get past Google there.

- If you use Telegram's Keep-Alive Service instead of push, messages no longer wait until you open the app. Android stopped that service about a minute after you left Telegram. Now it runs with a quiet notification and keeps going. A new switch under `Repair Firebase push registration`, `Keep the Keep-Alive Service running`, is on by default and only matters while Keep-Alive Service is on in Telegram's own settings. (#50, #54)

- `Keep deleted messages` now saves a kept photo, and any kept file or video up to 20 MB, the moment the sender deletes it. Before, a photo you hadn't opened yet just spun forever, because Telegram can't fetch a deleted message's file later. (#2)

- `Disable update checks` now hides the Update Telegram bar even when Telegram found the update before you turned the switch on. The bar used to stay, since Telegram only forgets an update when a later check comes back empty. (#60)

- With `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` on, the photos and videos Telegram downloads no longer fill up the phone's gallery. The folder now gets a .nomedia file, so the gallery only shows what you save to it yourself. (#60)

- `Hide greeting stickers` now also hides the custom sticker a Premium or Business user picks for their intro, the one you see when you open an empty chat with them. Only the preview of your own intro, while you edit it, keeps its sticker. (#56)

- In the `Side menu`, New Message has a pencil beside it again. Telegram 13 turned the old message icon into an eye, so the row looked like it would show you something.

Other changes

- Moved to Telegram 13.2. telegram.org's build is 13.2.0 (version code 72809) and the Google Play build is 13.2.1 (version code 72911). The 13.1 builds aren't supported anymore, so update Telegram before you patch.

- `Hide the reaction picker` now covers the bubble of reactions that pops up over a selected message too, so tapping a post to pick it for a reply or a forward can't land on a reaction.

- `Hide picked chats` now also takes hidden chats out of the forward picker, the share sheet and quick share. Saved Messages always stays in those lists.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.5.0 or newer. 0.0.23 only needed 2.3.0, so update Manager first if that's what you patched with.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get the right Telegram. From Google Play that's 13.2.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72911), which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. From telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) it's 13.2.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72809). The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from 0.0.23? Get 13.2 from the same place you got 13.1 (Google Play or telegram.org), patch it and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. Your settings and chats stay. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. On phones where Firebase notifications don't come through, try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy. It turns those two on for you unless you've set them yourself.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The Ways in section on that page decides which of those (plus the side menu row and the icon shortcut) stay.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

What was checked

All 2048 runtime tests passed locally, and all 625 patch tests passed too (162 unit tests and 463 that patch the real Telegram APKs), along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 69 patches applied without forcing to telegram.org's Telegram 13.2.0 (version code 72809) and to the Google Play build of 13.2.1 (version code 72911). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, resource table, native libraries and zip alignment.

Both builds were patched from this exact bundle and installed over the HushTelegram already on a Galaxy S25, without clearing its data. Both were signed in to Telegram. On each one the walk opened Telegram's Settings, Privacy, Folders and Themes pages and a channel, then every section of the HushTelegram settings and the Changed switches page. That's 22 screens per build, with no crash and no problem found on either.

The new `Allow screenshots in chats that don't allow saving` switch was checked on the same phone. With it off, a bot message that blocks saving and a channel with Restrict saving content both came out black in screenshots, same as stock Telegram. With it on, both showed normally.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.17
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.17 has 22 patches for Threads 454.0.0.54.79 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only, on all eight APKMirror variants. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.2.0, so you need Morphe Manager 2.4.0 or newer. Update Threads to 454 before you patch.

Two new patches. `Filter comments` hides replies that match words or sites you list, and `Show exact post times` swaps 3h and 2d for the real date and time. The settings got the same look as the other Hush packages, and they come in Italian, Korean and Traditional Chinese now too.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#15](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/15) found videos that Save couldn't get. Text posts that show a video from another post save that post's video or carousel now.
- [#16](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/16) found that sharing a post to a patched Messenger did nothing. The Messenger tile in the share sheet opens it now, like More > Messenger already did.
- [#18](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/discussions/18) asked how to hide the HushThreads row in Threads' settings. Each way into HushThreads settings has its own switch now, under Pause, backup and diagnostics, and the last one that's on stays on.
- [#19](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/pull/19) asked for Threads 454 on every APKMirror variant. That's what this release patches, the ARMv7 and x86 builds included.
- [#20](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/20) hit a patching failure in `Sanitize sharing links` on the 32-bit builds. Patching goes through on those now.
- [#21](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/pull/21) is @Cuhosuaxemay's `Filter comments` patch. Its switches and your word list are in the new Comments section of HushThreads settings.

## Threads

- New `Show exact post times` patch. Posts and replies show the date and time they went up instead of 3h or 2d, in your phone's 12 or 24-hour format, and TalkBack reads that same time out. It's in Manager's default selection, but its switch under Posts in HushThreads settings starts off.
- New `Filter comments` patch, contributed by @Cuhosuaxemay in #21. Replies to a post that match words or domains you list are left out before Threads builds its rows from them, so a spam reply ending in a shop link never shows. A reply and the replies shown under it are checked as one. A second switch under it also hides any reply with a web link, and a bare site name like shopee.vn goes in your list instead. Both start off, the matching ignores letter case, and the replies that stay keep their order. The switches and the list are in a new Comments section in HushThreads settings.
- The HushThreads settings look like the other Hush packages' now. The logo and name sit at the top and scroll away under the top bar. Each section opens in place on the main page instead of on a page of its own, and Pause moved up into the bar. A toggle under search shows every setting in one long list. Support at the bottom has Report a problem, a Restart Threads button and the Ko-fi link, and the build line sits under everything in small type.
- HushThreads settings and messages come in Italian, Korean and Traditional Chinese now. Phones set to Chinese for Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macau get the Traditional Chinese, which started from the translation NikolaJyun made in their fork.
- A section near the bottom of the settings opens with its first setting in view. Before, its settings went in below the edge of the screen, so it looked like the tap did nothing.
- Each way into HushThreads settings has its own switch under Pause, backup and diagnostics now, so you can take away the app icon shortcut, the row in Threads' settings or the long press on the logo. The last one that's on stays on, so there's always a way back in, and App info opens the settings whichever ones you keep. The row only counts on a Threads build that can show it. Asked for in #18.
- HushThreads now patches Threads 454.0.0.54.79 only, for all eight APKMirror variants across arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and x86, including the ARMv7 and x86 builds APKMirror added a day after release. The build is matched by version name, not pinned to one code, so a reupload of the same version works too. Update Threads to 454 before you patch, and use Morphe Manager 2.4.0 or newer. v0.0.16 is the last release for 452.0.0.50.64.
- HushThreads builds on Morphe patcher 2.2.0 now, so patching needs Morphe Manager 2.4.0 or newer. Older Managers refuse the bundle. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 2.0.0 or newer.
- Patching goes through on Threads builds that keep a shared link, a post or a long press override in a high register. `Sanitize sharing links` and the Copy text hook used to stop the whole run there, and 454's ARMv7 and x86 builds do it with Share to Instagram's link. Their hooks now read a copy of the value. Reported in #20.
- Save photos and videos now works on text posts that show a video from somewhere else. When a post has no media of its own, the Save row finds the post it links, quotes or reposts, and saves that post's video or carousel under that post's details. A post's own media still comes first.
- The share sheet's Messenger tile opens a re-signed Messenger now, same as More > Messenger always did. Threads' launcher only accepts Meta's own signature and the tile ignored the refusal, so nothing happened. Every tile in that sheet falls back the same way. It's part of `Restore screens on re-signed builds`, with no switch.
- Patched 32-bit Threads starts normally on the ARMv7 and x86 variants whose manifest asks for extracted native libraries. Merging the bundle compresses those libraries, and Threads tried to read them straight out of the APK. It loads them from the folder Android unpacked them to now.
- A crash in Threads' first minute is kept now, so the next diagnostic report has its stack trace, the Threads build and which switches were on. Safe mode used to count those crashes without keeping any of them. A crash later on is kept only while Debug logging is on, and an error Threads recovers from on a background thread leaves the earlier crash in place. `Clear diagnostic data` removes a kept crash too.
- Hide ads and Hide suggested users now also clean up For You when Threads keeps it in its spool cache. On some accounts Threads stores For You there instead of in the feed cache, and pages that went that way skipped both filters. A diagnostic report counts spool pages separately, so it shows which cache your For You uses.
- Hide ads also catches an ad Threads slips into a For You page you already have. Threads places some ads into the page it's holding instead of sending them with a new one, and those never passed through either filter. A diagnostic report counts the inserted items it checked and the ads it kept out.
- Hide ads and Hide suggested users also cover the other ways Threads writes For You into its cache. Refreshes, the cold-start page and some paging write their posts in directly instead of through the usual page merge, so on either cache those skipped both filters. So did a single post or card Threads adds, slots in after a post, or swaps in for one it already has. A diagnostic report counts these writes on their own.
- Hide suggested users also takes away the row of accounts to follow that For You puts under a post right after you follow its author. Threads puts that row together on the phone, without the server's suggestion tag, so it never matched the filter. A diagnostic report counts it with the other suggestion cards.
- When Hide ads or Hide suggested users breaks on one of For You's cache writes, the diagnostic report names that write. Before, every failure there was blamed on the feed page, even when the page was fine.
- Patching stops with a clear error if a future Threads build answers For You's one-item writes with something other than its plain "done" value. Hide ads used to take whatever every write returned, and a lookalike could have slipped past it.
- The patch bundle is signed now. Morphe Manager shows who signed it when you add or update the source (`d0d2 eda0 b978 70da`), remembers that key, and won't take an update signed by anyone else. If someone swaps the file on the way to you, Manager refuses it. The README says how to check the key.

## Docs

- The README says where HushThreads really comes from. Someone's copy of this repo under another account offers a Windows download, and HushThreads has never shipped one.
- The README says what a Threads ban can reach and how to lower the risk, why passkey sign-in can't work on a patched Threads, what Android's 2027 developer verification changes for installs, and what `INSTALL_FAILED_NO_MATCHING_ABIS` means. The bug form names that error too, and the README now says how reports close.
- NOTICE and the Licenses page credit De-Vanced now. The list of supported Threads builds and the patch list generator came from there through tiktok-patches-for-morphe, and their headers used to point at ReVanced paths that never held either file.

## Tooling

- Before anything gets tagged, a release checks the signature on the bundle copy it's going to publish, which it takes right after the build so nothing else in the checkout can swap it. That copy has to match the checksum the build wrote, and its signature has to verify against the key in `morphe-signing.pub`. One that changed after it was signed stops the release there instead of reaching Morphe Manager. The fixture runs, the release receipt and the index update read that same copy too, so they describe the bundle that's tagged and not whatever a later build left in the checkout.
- The whole-app walk follows the new settings layout. It opens each section on the main page and folds it again, and it checks the one-list view from the toggle under search before putting the toggle back the way it was.
- Changelog entries don't open with a "Threads:" label anymore. HushThreads only patches Threads, so it repeated itself on every line. The release scripts stopped adding or asking for it, and they drop it from any bullet that still has one when a release is cut.
- The bundle signing key comes from `HUSHTHREADS_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY` first and `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` second, so a shell that kept another repo's key doesn't fail the key check.
- A fresh checkout builds again. Dependency verification was missing the hash for junit-bom 5.13.1's module file, so Gradle stopped before compiling anything unless that file was already trusted locally.
- A release walk ties the installed APK to the bundle and the inputs it was patched from. Publish checks its manifest and identity again, and wants every screen covered with a clean result. A walk on an install that was already on the phone needs that install's patch receipt, and a stale or incomplete one is refused.
- The release description fixtures test conflicting build claims in the current facts now, ahead of the historical notes.
- The notice mirror check waits 400 ms between requests, so it doesn't draw rate limits when other Hush repos check the same mirrors at the same time.
- Fixture tests keep what they work out per build in soft references, with a 3 GB heap, so every variant fits in one run.
- The whole-app walk waits for each screen and scrolls to the row it wants, so a slow phone no longer reads as a failed walk. It also patches the same default selection Morphe Manager does. It used to apply every patch, `Change version code` included, and that left the phone on a build number no ordinary build could install over.
- The signed-app contracts find their sites by strings and shape instead of naming one build's classes, since a release checks every variant. They'd fallen behind on the move off 452 and again on 454, and caught up both times. On 454 they follow the feed merge's extra parameter, analytics sites that Threads now jumps onto, share tiles spread over several lambdas, and videos that reach the player through a helper holding autoplay off.
